meta.title: House of Manna Funding Pipeline
meta.note: Internal management view. Date Added reflects when an opportunity was first added to this tracker, not when the application was submitted. Statuses reviewed Sept. 21, 2026 using current House of Manna records and available submission confirmations.

grants.nextAction: Await Truist Foundation status communication. Truist advised approximately 3–4 months after the grant-cycle deadline.
grants.notes: Submission confirmed by email on Sept. 18. Truist advised that status communication should arrive approximately 3–4 months after the grant-cycle deadline.

grants.opportunity: Youth Business, AI & Community Innovation Lab
grants.nextAction: Await Sparkplug Foundation board update; submission confirmation said the board would respond within two weeks.
grants.notes: LOI submitted Sept. 18, 2026. Sparkplug confirmation states the board will provide an update within two weeks and, if approved, invite House of Manna to submit a full application.

grants.nextAction: Await BCF decision.
grants.notes: BCF submission confirmation received Aug. 19. No decision email found as of Sept. 18.

grants.nextAction: Await Baltimore Community Foundation decision.
grants.notes: BCF submission confirmation received Sept. 11. No decision email found as of Sept. 18.

grants.opportunity: Community Opportunity Initiative — Regular Grant LOI
grants.nextAction: Closed. Revisit only with a materially different concept or stronger operating history.
grants.notes: Abell responded Sept. 15 that the LOI was not a good fit with the foundation's scope and areas of interest.

grants.opportunity: Baltimore Neighborhood Food Access Pilot — Small Grant
grants.nextAction: Await Abell Foundation Small Grants decision.
grants.notes: Abell Foundation Small Grant application submitted Sept. 14, 2026. Application ID 2744593. This is separate from the declined regular-grant LOI.

grants.nextAction: Closed for the current concept.
grants.notes: Goldseker responded Sept. 14 that the project was not a fit for current grantmaking.

grants.nextAction: Log in to the M&T Versaic portal and verify whether the Community Food Access Program application was actually submitted. No submission-confirmation email was found in the connected House of Manna inbox.
grants.notes: M&T Versaic account was created Sept. 12, 2026. The connected House of Manna inbox contains account-registration emails but no application-submission confirmation, so the tracker no longer treats this as submitted until portal status is verified.

grants.nextAction: Await Whole Foods Market Store Giving review and decision.
grants.notes: House of Manna completed the Whole Foods Store Giving application. Benevity eligibility and EFT setup were approved Sept. 18, 2026.

grants.nextAction: Await response to the U.S. charity eligibility inquiry before submitting a grant application.
grants.notes: International applicants must receive approval before applying. Eligibility inquiry emailed Sept. 18; no reply found yet.

grants.opportunity: Community Facility, Food Access & Learning Infrastructure
grants.nextAction: Await France-Merrick Foundation response to the LOI.
grants.notes: House of Manna's LOI for cold storage, refrigeration, learning technology, and related program infrastructure was submitted. The concept discloses that House of Manna operates from a shared-use church facility.

grants.nextAction: Complete Spark Good / third-party verification and submit to relevant local facilities.
grants.notes: Account verification activity was found, but no grant-submission confirmation was found.

grants.opportunity: Food Lion Feeds Grant / Food Access Support
grants.nextAction: Complete Maryland Food Bank partnership / Feeding America affiliation before revisiting.
grants.notes: Maryland Food Bank New Partner Interest Form was submitted Sept. 9. No partner-approval email was found. Food Lion Feeds grant applications are cycle-based and require qualifying feeding-network affiliation. The linked official Food Lion Feeds page is the recurring entry point for application-cycle information.

grants.opportunity: Baltimore Healthy Food Access & Family Wellness Pilot
grants.nextAction: Begin application and frame food insecurity as a social driver of health.
grants.notes: Working concept: $20,000 request against a $30,000 pilot budget. No CareFirst application activity was found in email.

grants.nextAction: Revisit only if an eligible nonprofit collaboration is established.
grants.notes: The funding tier reviewed required collaboration with another eligible 501(c)(3). House of Manna chose not to pursue at this time.

grants.nextAction: Revisit after House of Manna files its first applicable 990-series return.
grants.notes: Foundation requires a completed 990-series filing and does not accept substitute financial statements for new organizations.

grants.nextAction: No action.
grants.notes: Reviewed and intentionally passed on Sept. 18.

grants.nextAction: Apply before Oct. 31, 2026 for gift-card support that can be used to purchase pantry products.
grants.notes: Direct fit for a new food pantry. ALDI's 2026 program offers $100–$1,000 gifts to qualified nonprofits, including food banks and pantries seeking to purchase essential products. 501(c)(3) documentation is required.

grants.nextAction: Await Costco review. Costco's confirmation says it will contact House of Manna by email or letter in 4–6 weeks.
grants.notes: Costco received the House of Manna Community Food Access & Learning Infrastructure Project request on Sept. 19, 2026. Reference #2026090470. Costco advised a 4–6 week review window.

grants.nextAction: Submit a contribution request for pantry food, gift cards, or project support; allow at least six weeks.
grants.notes: Harris Teeter lists local food banks as a primary charitable priority and accepts requests from registered 501(c)(3) organizations. Requests may be for cash, product, or gift cards. Proposals above $5,000 are reviewed annually and should reach Harris Teeter by Aug. 1.

grants.nextAction: Monitor the Weis Markets proposal account. Weis requests no follow-up calls or emails and will post status through the account.
grants.notes: Weis Markets confirmed receipt of the House of Manna Community Food Access Program charitable request on Sept. 20, 2026. The request is under Community Relations review.

grants.nextAction: Complete the Wegmans donation request and submit it. The request is being prepared for product donations and grocery gift cards through the Hunt Valley store.
grants.notes: Wegmans account created and donation request started Sept. 20, 2026. Application is not yet marked submitted.

grants.nextAction: Apply for weekly recurring pickup of unsold bread, bagels, and baked goods from a nearby Panera.
grants.notes: Panera is always accepting applications. Eligible organizations include registered 501(c)(3)s and religious organizations that distribute donated products to people in need. Participating organizations must commit to weekly, continuous pickup and distribution.

grants.nextAction: Hand-deliver House of Manna Neighborhood Shares partnership letters and nonprofit packet to the Donation Coordinator / Neighborhood Shares lead at the Elkridge and Towson stores; ask about recurring food-recovery partnership availability.
grants.notes: House of Manna prepared store-specific Neighborhood Shares partnership letters for Trader Joe's Elkridge Store #658 and Towson Store #649. This outreach targets recurring surplus-food recovery rather than the separate one-time annual product-donation process.

grants.nextAction: Await Sprouts review and decision. If Sprouts provides a review timeline or status update, record it in the tracker.
grants.notes: Sprouts Donation Request Application for the House of Manna Community Food Access Program completed and submitted Sept. 21, 2026. Request includes food/grocery product support and sponsorship materials.

grants.nextAction: Monitor the 2027 grant cycle and cultivate the Baltimore-area Sprouts relationship in advance.
grants.notes: Sprouts grants support nutrition access, nutrition education, and wellness. Recent grants have ranged from $5,000 to $10,000. House of Manna is geographically eligible because Sprouts operates multiple Maryland stores. Some larger Healthy Communities / Impact grants are invitation-only. Sprouts Healthy Communities Foundation grant cycles open periodically. The linked Foundation page is the official entry point for the grant program and application when a cycle is open.

grants.nextAction: Prepare the Community Food Access Program application now and return to Target's Community Engagement Funds page in April 2027 when Cycle 1 applications reopen.
grants.notes: Target Community Engagement Funds grants range from $1,000 to $15,000. House of Manna is eligible as a 501(c)(3) public charity. Best initial fit: Thriving Families - Basic Needs, using the Community Food Access Program. The 2026 Cycle 2 window closed Sept. 4, 2026; Target instructs applicants to return in April 2027 for Cycle 1.

grants.nextAction: Complete NPO Hub readiness and monitor for 2027 Basic Needs application dates.
grants.notes: Bank of America explicitly funds hunger and basic-needs organizations and accepts applications during posted RFP cycles. Organizations must register with NPO Hub and accept ACH payments. The 2026 Basic Needs cycle ran Feb. 2–Mar. 2.

grants.nextAction: Submit an unsolicited inquiry focused on Baltimore food access, nonprofit capacity, and family stability.
grants.notes: T. Rowe Price Foundation primarily supports nonprofits in Baltimore and provides unrestricted general-operating grants. Most grants are invitation-only, but the Foundation states that it reviews unsolicited proposals submitted by inquiry form or email. T. Rowe Price Foundation is primarily invitation-only. The linked official Foundation page is the correct entry point for program information and relationship development; there is no general public grant application.

grants.nextAction: Prepare a one-page request emphasizing Baltimore food access, nutrition, and community health; submit to McCormick's CDC.
grants.notes: McCormick accepts first-time charitable requests from qualifying nonprofits and prioritizes communities where its employees live and work. Health and Wellness is a stated focus area, and McCormick has a longstanding Maryland Food Bank relationship.

grants.nextAction: Submit a BGE operating-company inquiry under local vitality / family resilience and describe the food-access project.
grants.notes: Exelon invites new organizations to review operating-company programs and use an inquiry form. Its local-vitality giving supports families, resilience, and stronger communities. BGE serves central Maryland, including Baltimore.

grants.opportunity: United for Good Nonprofit Resiliency Grant
grants.nextAction: Monitor for the next resiliency/basic-needs funding opportunity and prepare a food-access sustainability case.
grants.notes: The 2026 program awarded $2,500–$25,000 to Central Maryland 501(c)(3)s supporting basic needs. Baltimore Hunger Project and other community-based organizations were among 2026 recipients. The current cycle is closed.

grants.nextAction: Develop a youth nutrition / food-literacy component connected to the pantry and monitor for the next PLAY 60 cycle.
grants.notes: PLAY 60 provides up to $10,000 to Maryland 501(c)(3)s for youth ages 5–18 programs focused on physical fitness and/or nutrition education. It is not a direct food-purchasing grant, so the best House of Manna angle is youth nutrition education tied to food access.

grants.opportunity: True Inspiration Awards — Caring Through Food
grants.nextAction: Build outcomes and a local Chick-fil-A operator relationship before the next application cycle opens.
grants.notes: True Inspiration Awards grants range from $30,000 to $350,000. The Caring Through Food category supports programs addressing hunger and food insecurity among children and families. The 2027 application cycle is closed, so this is a future-cycle target.

grants.nextAction: Submit a rolling LOI focused on food access and, secondarily, entrepreneurship / farm-to-fork skills.
grants.notes: Conagra accepts one online LOI from eligible U.S. 501(c)(3) public charities on a rolling basis. Its core focus areas include food insecurity, food access, nutrition education, cooking skills, and entrepreneurial skills connected to the farm-to-fork economy.

grants.nextAction: Approach local BJ's community leadership and explore whether House of Manna can enter the foundation's hunger-relief pipeline as capacity grows.
grants.notes: BJ's Charitable Foundation lists Hunger Relief as a core giving pillar and has funded school pantries, food banks, equipment, and direct-access food programs, including a $50,000 grant to the Maryland Food Bank. Public materials do not show a simple open application path, so relationship-building is the first step. BJ's current charitable giving is primarily relationship- and team-member-nomination driven; no general public grant application was identified. The linked official purpose page is the best current entry point.

grants.opportunity: Community Impact Awards / Food for Good Partnership
grants.nextAction: Identify a PepsiCo employee advocate or explore Food for Good partnership outreach rather than submitting an unsolicited funding proposal.
grants.notes: PepsiCo's 2026 Community Impact Awards provided $5,000 employee-nominated grants to 100 local nonprofits, including organizations expanding food access. Food for Good invites partnership conversations, but PepsiCo states that it does not accept unsolicited proposals for funding. PepsiCo Foundation states that it does not accept unsolicited funding proposals. The linked Foundation page includes Food for Good partnership information and contact options.

grants.opportunity: Hunger Priority / Local Store Gift Card Support
grants.nextAction: Request local-store gift-card support now and build toward an invitation to a larger hunger-focused RFP.
grants.notes: Safeway Foundation's Eastern region includes Maryland and lists Hunger as a priority. Larger foundation grants are invitation-only through RFPs, but local store directors may consider written gift-card requests of $50 or less from eligible nonprofits. Safeway Foundation's larger Eastern-region grant opportunities are generally RFP/invitation driven. The linked official application-process page explains the online process; local store gift-card requests are handled through store leadership.

grants.opportunity: Food Rescue Bank Partnership / Recurring Food Distribution
grants.nextAction: Await Baltimore team follow-up. The confirmation page indicated contact within about 3 weeks; the submitted form also notes a long waitlist.
grants.notes: New Partnership Inquiry submitted Sept. 20, 2026 for a new food distribution and recurring perishable/non-perishable food support. So What Else notes that submission places House of Manna on a long waitlist and does not guarantee service.

grants.opportunity: New Partner Interest / Food Pantry Partnership
grants.nextAction: Await Maryland Food Bank partner review and onboarding instructions.
grants.notes: Maryland Food Bank confirmed receipt of House of Manna's New Partner Interest Form on Sept. 9, 2026.
